## The Question

- Open with the thing the audience already believes, so the paper has
  something to push against.
- State the question in one sentence. If it takes two, it is two questions.
- Say why it has not been answered: the data did not exist, the variation was
  not there, the identification was not available.

::: {.takeaway title="What this paper changes"}
One sentence the audience should still be able to repeat in the corridor an
hour later. Write it before you write the slides.
:::

## Headline Estimates

::: {.stats}
- **0.41 s.d.** the effect at the median
- **1 in 4** attenuation from measurement error
- **62,400** unit-years in the panel
:::

Put the answer on the third slide. A seminar audience decides in five minutes
whether to keep listening, and a paper that withholds its result until slide
thirty is asking them to wait on trust.

# Design

## Three Contributions

::: {.contributions}
1. **The first thing the paper does** One sentence on why it matters. Keep
   the claim narrow enough that you could defend it alone.
2. **The second thing** Something the existing literature assumes rather than
   estimates, and that you can now measure.
3. **The third thing** Where the estimate varies, and why that variation is
   the interesting part rather than a nuisance.
:::

## The Specification

$$
  y_{it} = \alpha_i + \delta_t + \beta D_{it}
    + \gamma \sum_{j \neq i} w_{ij} D_{jt} + \varepsilon_{it}
$$

where $D_{it}$ is treatment and $w_{ij}$ a weight on the link between $i$ and
$j$. Say what each term is doing in words before you defend it, and name the
one coefficient the talk is about.

::: {.caveat}
State the identifying assumption here rather than in the appendix. The
audience is going to ask; answering first is cheaper than being asked.
:::

## What It Adds Up To

::: {.takeaway title="The result"}
Restate the headline in the same words you used on slide three. An audience
that hears it twice remembers it; one that hears two versions remembers
neither.
:::

- The mechanism, in one line.
- Where the estimate does not hold, said plainly [@callaway2021].
- What you would need to go further, which is also your next paper.
